witness.text:
Both numbers
are true, nobody lied, and the space
between them is the most expensive piece
of misinformation in your financial
life.

comparisons.rationale: Opens with a relatable scene (the statement at the kitchen table), a scroll-stop contradiction ($44,000 versus a "record $167,000") and a contrarian snapback that both numbers are true, with a promise to find the man hiding in the gap.
comparisons.uncertainty: Single analyst reading of stored untimed text; no audio, timing, CTR or retention data.

witness.text:
When somebody says the
average American, they almost always
mean the mean.

comparisons.rationale: The first minute states the topic, the audience stake and the core idea (mean versus median) in plain language; emotional tone is wry and sympathetic. Clarity high.
comparisons.uncertainty: Single analyst reading of stored untimed text; no audio, timing, CTR or retention data. First-30-second proxy is the first ~700 characters.

witness.text: Shocking Finance Stats Of The Average Person

comparisons.rationale: Title promises "shocking" statistics about the average person; the opening instead promises a reframing (the average is misleading). The expectation is met in spirit (shocking numbers follow) but redirected within the first minute.
comparisons.uncertainty: Expectation match inferred from text; viewer behaviour unmeasured; inferred only.

witness.text:
Now, I promised you one number
worse than all the others.

comparisons.rationale: The held-back worst number is delivered at the net-worth section, so the opening promise is paid off, and the "man in the gap" (Gerald) arrives as promised. The title/thumbnail promise of "shocking stats" is delivered across the stats sections.
comparisons.uncertainty: Thumbnail alignment judged from text and image only; the thumbnail calculator 0.0674 has no script counterpart.

witness.text:
I'm holding it until the end
because you need everything else first
for it to land.

comparisons.rationale: Explicit open loop planted in the first minute and closed at the net-worth reveal, with a mid-video reminder that a character will be introduced; strong loop discipline.
comparisons.uncertainty: Loop pairing is inferred from text order; retention effect not evaluable.

Now, you're
probably thinking, "Well, Nick, this is
all very grim, but maybe things are
actually getting better and you're just
cherry-picking the worst numbers you

comparisons.rationale: Clear BUT pivot (the steelman) followed by a THEREFORE (the 401k default explains the 86%), and elsewhere "Which brings me to" causal links; mostly cause-and-effect, with a long stats run in the middle that is more list than chain.
comparisons.uncertainty: Transition counts are descriptive; ASR text may drop or alter connectives.

The median
is the guy standing in the exact middle
of the line.

comparisons.rationale: Complex idea (mean versus median) explained in everyday language with a concrete room example; but the arithmetic in that example is wrong (see packet claim C01).

witness.text:
the average income
in that room is just under 1 and 1/2
million dollars.

comparisons.rationale: Specific numbers are present but this one contradicts its own inputs ($1,045,000). The reference criterion rewards specificity; the fact-check shows specificity here is inaccurate.
comparisons.uncertainty: Specificity is not accuracy; see packet claim C01.

witness.text:
This is
exactly what we dig into inside our
school community where I run the real
numbers instead of the headline versions
of them.

comparisons.rationale: Soft CTA to a free community placed after the emotional peak and before the payoff, plus actions that end the video; no next-video bridge.
